GraceRequirements.Status: Approved product baseline; implementation and physical-device gates remain separate follow-up work.
GraceRequirements.Purpose: OpenWearSync is a one-way, lossless transfer system for large Samsung Voice Recorder files from a Galaxy Watch running Wear OS to a Windows PC over a local Wi-Fi topology.
GraceRequirements.Problem: Continuous background synchronization caused unacceptable watch battery drain when the Windows receiver was unavailable. OpenWearSync uses bounded, user-visible or OS-cooperative sessions instead of a persistent synchronizer.

Users.User: Wear OS owner who selects or schedules eligible recordings for transfer.
Windows owner who pairs watches, runs the receiver, selects a destination, and inspects transfer history.
Maintainer who needs durable protocol, security, energy, and evidence contracts.

ProductBoundary.Direction: Only the watch sends recordings to the Windows receiver. The phone hotspot may forward packets but is not an application relay or data processor.
ProductBoundary.Transport: Recording payloads use Wi-Fi and an authenticated encrypted session. Bluetooth, cloud hosting, mobile-data relay, and mandatory phone software are outside the product.
ProductBoundary.Source: Samsung Voice Recorder files remain on the watch unless a future, separately approved deletion feature is introduced; this baseline never deletes originals.
ProductBoundary.Destination: The receiver owns its configured destination directory and publishes immutable final-file identity through the storage registry.

SupportedTopology.Topology: Galaxy Watch client to Samsung Galaxy S25 Ultra hotspot to Windows PC receiver.
Private local LAN where the watch can reach the receiver by TCP or HTTPS.
SupportedTopology.Constraint: Hotspot station-to-station unicast and multicast forwarding are unverified and must be demonstrated on target hardware.
SupportedTopology.Fallback: Use a saved authenticated endpoint or a manually entered local address when discovery is unavailable and routing still permits reachability.

TransferInvariants.NetworkDelivery: Network delivery is at-least-once. Reconnects, retries, duplicate requests, and reordered requests are expected protocol inputs.
TransferInvariants.DurableOutcome: Exactly-once durable file outcome means a logical recording produces one committed receiver artifact and one consistent registry result, even when protocol messages are delivered more than once.
TransferInvariants.Acknowledgement: Receiver acknowledgements describe checkpoint data durably persisted in the registry and recoverable after a crash; in-memory bytes are never acknowledged as durable.
TransferInvariants.Resumption: After reconnect or receiver restart, the receiver returns durable ranges and the watch resends only data that is not recorded as durable, subject to bounded retry policy.
TransferInvariants.Integrity: Every chunk is length- and digest-checked, the manifest is revalidated at completion, and the receiver records a final content fingerprint before atomic publication.
TransferInvariants.Collision: Existing destination files are never silently overwritten; a collision is rejected or resolved by a deterministic safe name.

RecordingReadiness.StableFile: A recording is eligible only after a conservative stable-size and metadata policy says it is not actively growing. Stability is a heuristic and must not be presented as proof of recorder completion.
RecordingReadiness.ChangingFile: A file that changes during manifest or chunk reads is deferred or version-restarted and is never reported as a successful complete recording.
RecordingReadiness.AccessGate: Real hardware must demonstrate that a non-root third-party Wear OS application can open and read a Samsung Voice Recorder recording without relying on ADB shell visibility.
RecordingReadiness.ReadPath: MediaStore, SAF, or another permitted descriptor path is selected only after the target watch and firmware access test records the supported mechanism.

SecurityRequirements.Pairing: Initial pairing requires a user-confirmed one-time code through a reviewed PAKE-style or equivalent exchange and persists a revocable receiver identity pin.
SecurityRequirements.Authentication: Only explicitly paired watch identities may create or continue upload sessions.
SecurityRequirements.Encryption: Control and payload traffic use TLS or an equally reviewed authenticated encrypted channel; discovered hostnames and IP addresses are locators, not identities.
SecurityRequirements.Replay: Session identity, sequence, and completion checks reject replayed or stale messages.
SecurityRequirements.ResourceLimits: Manifests, chunk counts, chunk sizes, concurrent sessions, path components, disk reservations, and request time are bounded before expensive work starts.
SecurityRequirements.PathSafety: Receiver paths are derived from its configured destination and a safe display name; traversal, absolute paths, device names, and arbitrary destinations are rejected.
SecurityRequirements.Secrets: Pairing keys and pins use platform-protected storage and are not committed to the repository or emitted in ordinary diagnostics.

EnergyRequirements.Idle: True idle has no app-owned persistent socket, Wi-Fi request, wake lock, file polling loop, or perpetual multicast listener on the watch.
EnergyRequirements.Session: Long transfers run only in a user-visible foreground or OS-supported scheduled context and retain a hard deadline, cancellation path, and energy eligibility policy.
EnergyRequirements.Retry: Discovery and reconnect retries are bounded by attempt count, backoff, and session deadline; an unavailable PC does not create an overnight loop.
EnergyRequirements.Cleanup: Success, cancellation, timeout, error, receiver loss, and thermal stop release sockets, callbacks, network requests, subscriptions, and wake resources before returning to idle.
EnergyRequirements.Measurement: Release approval requires matched on-device battery and temperature trials. The proposed acceptance target is median excess overnight idle drain no greater than 2 percentage points over 8 hours, pending calibration on target hardware.

AcceptanceGates.Gate: Non-privileged Samsung Voice Recorder read on a real Galaxy Watch.
Watch-to-Windows TCP or HTTPS reachability through the S25 Ultra hotspot, with client-isolation behavior recorded.
Explicit binding to the selected Android Wi-Fi Network rather than Bluetooth or whichever network happens to be default.
Discovery behavior with multicast permitted, blocked, and changed addresses; saved and manual endpoint fallback when routing permits.
Interrupted transfer at a known progress point, receiver crash or restart, corrupt chunk, duplicate delivery, disk-full condition, and final atomic commit.
Pairing, revocation, identity pinning, replay rejection, traversal rejection, and bounded oversized-request behavior.
Cleanup evidence for success, cancellation, timeout, failure, and thermal stop plus matched idle battery and temperature measurements.

ConfirmedFacts.Fact: Galaxy Watch recordings have been observed through ADB under a Recordings/Voice Recorder path.
Syncthing-Fork previously transferred the recordings but created unacceptable sustained activity when its peer was unavailable.
The S25 Ultra hotspot is the required primary network topology and is not a processing intermediary.
The target direction is shared Rust transfer logic with Kotlin platform and user-interface integration on Wear OS and Windows.

UnverifiedAssumptions.Assumption: Third-party app access to Samsung recorder content is available through a supported non-root API on the target firmware.
The hotspot forwards station-to-station unicast and, where applicable, multicast discovery.
Native Rust sockets can bind to the Kotlin-selected Android Network on all supported Wear OS versions.
Minimum OS versions, package distribution, exact pairing UX, cryptographic crate selection, session duration, and numeric throughput targets will be set after review and device measurement.

NonGoals.Item: Syncthing protocol compatibility or generic bidirectional directory synchronization.
Bluetooth payload transport, cloud service, mobile-data relay, or compulsory phone companion.
Uploading growing recordings, transcoding, transcription, or deleting originals by default.
Throwaway intermediate implementations before the approved target architecture is built.
